I've been farming this land for 30 years. I know Quzhou well — the soil, the rainfall patterns, the groundwater table. My children work in the city now, so labor is tighter than it used to be. That shapes everything I do.

**My thinking:**

My 13.1 mu splits naturally: 8.1 mu stays in the wheat-maize rotation, 5.0 mu in cotton. I won't expand cotton this year. At 59, picking season wears on me, and I can't count on family help like I used to. The wheat-maize system is more mechanized — I can hire a combine for harvest and move on.

For **wheat** this coming winter, I'll use an improved variety — something from the Jimai or Kenong lines that the county extension has been promoting. I apply base fertilizer before sowing: phosphorus and potassium go in all at once, nitrogen split between base and a topdress at jointing. I'll irrigate three times: once pre-winter to help roots establish, once at jointing, once at grain filling. Three pesticide passes — herbicide early, then aphids and powdery mildew closer to heading. Rotary tillage after maize harvest to incorporate the straw.

For **summer maize**, I go straight into no-till right after wheat combine. Hybrid seed,郑单958 type or similar. I push nitrogen a bit because maize responds well on my loam soil. Two irrigations — one around tasseling if we get a dry July, one at grain fill. Two pesticide passes cover the main threats.

For **cotton**, I plough in spring, transplant in late April. Bt hybrid seed cuts my insecticide burden but I still spray for aphids and spider mites — five passes is realistic. Four irrigations spread across the long season. I give cotton more potassium because fiber quality depends on it.

I'm not chasing maximum yield on every crop. I'm chasing stable income with manageable labor. My well is still reliable, but I'm conscious of not overpumping — the water table here has dropped noticeably in my lifetime.
